engine.name: KinetiKa Simulator
engine.precedence: system/cfg first, user file second, later wins per key
engine.note: Sections below mirror the menu sections that exist in the simulator. effectiveKeys is exactly what the runtime reads today; every other key documents a feature and the status it has. The runtime reports at start-up any key inside physics, audio, assist, video and singleplayer that it does not read, so a typo cannot stay hidden. MODE SETUP takes its starting values from singleplayer.defaults below, falling back to defaultsForMode() in the code for whatever the file leaves out.

physics.note: Fixed simulation step in seconds, accepted range 1e-5..1.0; 1/120 is the compiled default.

assist.note: Driver aids applied from the setup at start-up only, 0..12.

settings.note: The three entries of the SETTINGS screen: every image option lives in the video page, the volumes in audio, the bindings in controls.

video.note: What this file drives at start-up: resolution, exposure, tonemap, ssao, ssr, ssgi with ssgiRadius and ssgiIntensity, motionBlur, vsync, frameLimit, anisotropicFiltering, particles, headPhysics, shadowMapSize and shadowCascades. The OPTIONS page applies fullscreen, resolution, vsync, ssao, ssr, motion blur, exposure, tonemap and master volume live and keeps them in memory; msaa, postProcessFilter and hdrOutput document that state instead of setting it - the pipelines are built with one sample, the ppfilter preset is the display pass's, and the swapchain decides HDR output.

sources.landsAs: resolution, fullscreen, vsync, frame limit, anisotropic, shadow map, AA samples
sources.note: Resolution, fullscreen and vsync switch the window and the swapchain; the frame limit paces the loop (0 = vsync only) and the anisotropy number caps the material samplers at the device limit. All of it comes from this file.
Exposure and the tone curve are read from this file at startup, applied after the post preset, and the page reads them back from the renderer.
Bloom is a real half-resolution pass - glare extract, blur H, blur V - feeding the display pass. Occlusion-driven lens flare is not implemented.

The bounce is gathered at half resolution by ssgiGather.frag into its own target and denoised with two gaussian axes before the deferred lighting pass samples it as binding 8 - that filter is what keeps a wide video.ssgiRadius smooth. video.ssgi turns it on (and switches the render path to deferred, because the forward path never runs that shader, off by default); video.ssgiRadius and video.ssgiIntensity tune footprint and strength. The two engine-side ssgi compute shaders build but nothing dispatches them.
Screen-space reflections exist; planar and mirror reflections do not.
Configurable cascade count (1..3) and map size, without per-frame retargeting.
Forward and deferred paths exist; the list of named modes does not.
The deferred path has its own gbuffer layout; per-material overrides are not loaded.
video.particles starts the ParticleSystem emitters and the billboard pass draws them; KS_PARTICLES=1 still forces them on for a capture.
The lighting pass reads rain intensity and track wetness from the weather every frame, and the drops and spray come from the particle emitters video.particles starts.
Tyres render as plain meshes: no deformation or flat-spot visuals.
A weather state drives sun and sky values; shader-level weather is absent.
The native display pass applies exposure, the tone curve and the ppfilter LUT; no external post-processing middleware is involved.
One window, one swapchain: no triple-head splitting or side-angle correction.
Longitudinal and lateral acceleration sway the cockpit head through a spring-damper; vertical suspension travel is not fed in yet.
A free orbit camera exists for the showroom and the menu backdrop.
Chase and cockpit views exist, without spring or offset tuning.
Two views exist and switch; its per-camera bookmarks are not read.
Onboard camera is fixed to the car's cockpit node; no FOV or offset tuning.

audio.note: master is the only audio key the runtime reads; the engine, wind and environment levels are driven per frame by the session and the showroom channel starts with the simulator, so engineVolume, environmentVolume, showroomAmbience and showroomMusic document that behaviour rather than act as preferences.

sources.note: Master is a real setting. Engine, wind, tyre and opponent levels are driven per frame by the session, so they are not exposed as preferences.
The showroom plays ambience and music with declick and headroom; there is no playlists screen.
Keyboard only: seven actions, each captured and swapped so two actions never share a key. Arrow keys stay reserved.
Partially implemented: see landsAs for the part that exists.
Partially implemented: see landsAs for the part that exists.

sources.landsAs: SINGLE PLAYER rows (same eight modes, same order)
sources.note: One row per entry of singleplayer.modes, in that order; the player's own settings.json overrides the list and an unknown name is reported instead of started. Each row opens MODE SETUP and START SESSION hands the chosen values to the loop.

sources.landsAs: MODE SETUP screen (laps, AI cars, clock, garage start)
sources.note: One screen per mode with steps of one lap, one AI car and five minutes, a garage-start toggle and a summary of what is about to start. The values begin at singleplayer.defaults for that mode and fall back to defaultsForMode() for the fields the file leaves out; the screen is where a single session is then adjusted.

Car and track come from the chosen content; the MODE SETUP screen sets the laps, the AI cars, the session clock and whether the player starts in the garage. AI level and a fixed setup are not exposed.
Applied from the setup at start-up only.
Car collisions are always on; the collision radius is fixed.
Gearbox, clutch and tyre model are the engine's own; the extra systems are not ported.

singleplayer.note: modes picks the SINGLE PLAYER rows; defaults sets what MODE SETUP starts from for each of them. Only the fields an entry carries are overridden, so laps alone leaves the AI count, the clock and the garage flag as they are; the user file merges over the system one key by key, and an unknown mode name is reported and ignored. Practice and qualifying minutes stay in the code.

sources.note: A notice is raised whether the host starts or refuses to.
No password, slot list or booking.
Partially implemented: see landsAs for the part that exists.
kssimserver.exe ships next to the simulator; there is no in-menu manager.
Career totals are kept and written to stats.json; there is no championship progression.
Implemented and driven by this section.
Upgrade packages cycle and apply; there is no per-parameter setup screen.
The showroom is a real scene (content/showrooms/industrial).
Discs glow with temperature; there is no glow texture or spark set.
Pit lane phases exist; the driver does not walk.
Surface names map to friction; per-surface effects are not rendered.
Fuel target and repair jobs are handed to the pit service.
The service runs when the car is stopped in the box; tyre compound choice is not implemented.
Size and sampling rate are read as documented defaults; autosave counts are not enforced per session type.
Scrolling list with the car folder name; class and year filters are declared but not applied.
Bodywork maps to the CARBODY material; paintable regions are not declared per car.
Layouts come from the track folder: trackSelect picks one, and the session loads its data with the meshes.
Positions, best lap, disqualification and finish state are shown per driver.
No export, no championship points.
Rounded cards, resume/restart/garage/settings/quit.
A photo mode with a free camera exists; its filters and depth of field do not.
Startup tiles open the sections directly.
No launcher page: the simulator opens on the tiles.
The header bar (clock, notifications, quick actions) is the part with a counterpart; no widget list.
Partially implemented: see landsAs for the part that exists.
The runtime is its own engine: there are no core switches to inherit.
The row opens a confirmation screen; the mode itself only logs.
Settings are written back before the window closes.
content/cars folders; kn5 meshes and power curves are read at load.
Partially implemented: see landsAs for the part that exists.
One showroom is installed; its preview grid does not exist.
Packaging::unpack is a stub that returns false: content is read in place from its folder (and from .zip reads done at load time), never extracted to disk.
